plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49]. The symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bidding strategy for n bidders with uniform values is to bid (n-1)/n times your value. With n=3, that's 2/3 of my value. My value is $22, so optimal bid ≈ $14.67. This balances winning probability against profit margin, maximizing expected long-run earnings.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. My value is $34, so optimal bid ≈ 34 × (2/3) ≈ 22.7. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive against other rational bidders using similar strategies.
